A successful sync does not mean a device recorded new measurements. Summaries are marked stale after 24 hours, when their day/time zone changes, or when source freshness is unknown. Missing sleep or heart-rate data is never treated as zero. Recorded heart-rate summaries are not resting heart rate or a recovery diagnosis.

FitnessBalance requests read-only access to steps, sleep sessions and heart-rate records. It reads these only during a sync you initiate, to show daily steps, recent sleep duration and recorded heart-rate summaries. It requests no background or historical-access permission.

Only summaries and their time windows are cached in private, account-specific storage on this device, excluded from Android backup. Raw records are not retained. This module does not upload health data to Firebase, analytics or another server, and does not write records into Health Connect.

The cache is overwritten by sync or removed using “Remove saved summaries from this device”. Uninstalling the app also removes it. Revoked data types are hidden and removed from the cache when access is next checked. Revoking Health Connect permission does not itself delete the original records from their source apps.

You can grant only the data types you choose and manage or revoke access in Health Connect. Without permission or source records, summaries remain unavailable. Food and exercise logging continue independently. Imported summaries never change calorie goals, nutrient targets, XP or logged exercise calories. With your separate opt-in on the Exercise page, fresh sleep summaries can suggest a shorter existing workout. The comparison baseline uses at least three previous comparable recorded days; source records may be incomplete. Baseline observations and up to 20 recommendation explanations are stored only on this device, excluded from backup. Disabling sleep suggestions or removing saved summaries removes this baseline and history.

These summaries are for personal tracking and are not a diagnosis or treatment recommendation.
